body: The first week of June brings a focus on food security, water sustainability, energy policy, and economic performance across the Middle East

* Striving for Stability: What Lies Ahead for the MENA Region in 2026. * Med this Week Middle East and North Africa. Today, we shed light on the main trends and issues to watch in the MENA countries in 2026. At the same time, 2025 marked the return of Donald Trump and the United States as a central actor in the Middle East. From investment-driven agreements with Gulf countries to renewed efforts at normalisation with Syria, and culminating in strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities as well as a leading role in the Gaza peace plan, the year confirmed **Washington’s renewed capacity to project power and influence** across the region. With elections scheduled in Morocco, Algeria, Lebanon and, most notably, Israel, alongside major multilateral gatherings such as COP31 in Antalya, the MENA region is once again set to **be at the centre of international attention**. “In 2026, the Arab Middle East and North Africa (MENA) may be less permeable than a decade ago – but also more fragile.

# Middle East and North Africa (MENA). Across the Middle East and North Africa (MNA) region, droughts, earthquakes, water scarcity, and heat waves continue to hamper development efforts and adversely impact livelihoods and economies. Weather extremes, such as torrential rains and floods, affect tens of thousands each year—with many events occurring in contexts of fragility arising from conflict. Disaster recovery efforts have been underway in such countries, presenting more complex challenges and a need for coordinated efforts among additional development partners. Disaster risk reduction in urban areas remains a priority in this heavily urbanized region where many cities are significantly exposed to natural hazards.
